issues.description: The four exact analysis inputs named by the supplied code are absent from the assigned package inventory: CKM.dta, new_issues_emma.dta, CKM_local.dta, and CKM_congress.dta. No readable file, schema, or verified compatible retrieval route is present.

The datasheet describes historical source collection and manual construction of the analysis panel, including Single Audit city/county records, ZIP-to-district assignment, political membership/tenure, departure verification, bond issuer matching, and DOJ/court geographic linkage. It also names separate election data sources. The supplied do-file starts from prepared datasets and the datasheet-referenced Appendix D worked example is not included. The author-prepared CKM and new-issue files are the primary route; historic raw source origins are not separate mandatory inputs if compatible prepared files are supplied.

The do-file calls the bond merge input new_issues_emma.dta, while the datasheet says Thomson Reuters SDC Platinum records were hand-matched to Single Audit auditees by issuer name, state, city, and ZIP. The source/product relationship, issuer-to-government mapping, issue-year definition, and whether the prepared EMMA file is the intended deliverable are unresolved. Frozen catalog SDC new-issues metadata does not establish a compatible municipal issuer crosswalk.

The code’s actual time construction requires t−1 tenure/death/appropriation values, contiguous PC1 history for t−1 through t−4, and a t+1 PC1 value for the reputation measure. The broad FAC period is 1999–2016, but the required per-variable edge coverage and construction of precomputed pc1_finrep_lag/lead_rvotes in the two election inputs are not specified. Do not infer a minimum start year from the source filter.

The Table 7 and Table 8 branches load independent CKM_local.dta and CKM_congress.dta files. The datasheet traces local-official elections to OurCampaigns and congressional elections to MIT Election Data and Science Lab, but CKM Code.do does not create either analysis file or document the producer/identifier/period handoff for lead_rvotes, pc1_finrep_lag, and their distinct local versus congressional tenure inputs. Both supplied branches remain in the target.

All four input references use Windows [redacted-path-9842a853c665] paths. The documented Stata batch wrapper runs in the host working directory and requires relative or [redacted-path-ed5326351e1f] paths; the exact file references need a coherent relative staging root.
The Table 21 exclusion code names FA in the 12-state list, while the appendix specifies FL. This is a supported exact repair so the listed 12 states match the source description.

Stata 18 currently finds reghdfe 6.12.3, and the supplied code uses its older parenthetical IV specification plus the keepsin option. The PDF transcript records a prior run, but it does not identify the reghdfe release. Current syntax/option compatibility remains unverified; preserve the estimator, instrument, fixed effects, sample, and cluster specification.

On May 25, 2017, we downloaded House/Senate committee assignment and membership data

iii).

evidence.description: The datasheet documents geographic and political linkage history, manual issuer matching, and DOJ/court district mapping.
evidence.quote:
a. We use auditee ZIP code available from the Single Audit database to identify relevant
      congressional districts. As we mentioned in Item #2 above, we use the US Census historical
      mapping file between ZIP code and congressional districts to conduct this step. In case
      local governments report multiple ZIP code over time (mostly due to the relocation of their
      headquarters), we consider the ZIP code most commonly reported throughout the sample
      period. Also, if local governments report ZIP code that crosses congressional district
      boundaries, we remove these observations from our dataset.

   b. Using the House/Senate committee assignment and membership data, we identify two
      senators at the state-level and one house representative at congressional district-level for
      each local government. Next, we calculate the strength of their congressional
      representation based on their committee assignment and tenure. In Appendix D, we show
      this data step in detail using an example of Shelby County, Alabama.

   c. We use the House/Senate membership data to identify all politician departures. Next, we
      use Factiva and LexisNexis to verify the date of departure and the reason for departure to
      identify death and cabinet appointment cases. Finally, we verify the information about the
      deaths of Senators from U.S. Senate website.
      (https://www.senate.gov/senators/Biographical/necrology.htm).

   d. We hand-matched the data from Thomson Reuters to the Single Audit database by local
      government name using issuer (auditee) name, state, city, and zip code.

   e. We use geographical boundaries of U.S. Attorney’s Offices to establish a mapping between
      local governments and the number of convictions. The information about the boundaries
      of U.S. Attorney’s Office is available from the Offices of Attorneys of the U.S. Department
      of Justice (https://www.justice.gov/usao/find-your-united-states-attorney). Similarly, we
      use the information about the geographical boundaries of U.S. Court Districts to establish
      a mapping between local governments and the number of court cases. The information
      about     the    boundaries     of    U.S.    Court     Districts   is     available   from
      (https://www.uscourts.gov/federal-court-finder/search).

evidence.description: Tenure, death, and appropriation measures are lagged by one audityear before downstream analyses.
The code creates PC1 histories for four contiguous prior years and a one-year future PC1 used by downstream measures.
evidence.quote:
foreach i in pc1_finrep{
by dbkey1: gen lag_pc1_finrep  = pc1_finrep[_n-1] if audityear == audityear[_n-1] +1
by dbkey1: gen lag2_pc1_finrep = pc1_finrep[_n-2] if audityear == audityear[_n-2] +2
by dbkey1: gen lag3_pc1_finrep = pc1_finrep[_n-3] if audityear == audityear[_n-3] +3
by dbkey1: gen lag4_pc1_finrep = pc1_finrep[_n-4] if audityear == audityear[_n-4] +4
}
gen sum_pc1_finrep = lag_pc1_finrep + lag2_pc1_finrep + lag3_pc1_finrep + lag4_pc1_finrep
xtile pc1_finrep_rank = sum_pc1_finrep, nq(4)
gen low_finrep=1 if pc1_finrep_rank ==1
replace low_finrep=0 if missing(low_finrep)
foreach i in 610 59 48 37{ 
gen sum_tenure`i'_low_finrep=sum_tenure`i'_nolag*low_finrep
}
gen lead_fin=f.pc1_finrep

actions.description: Obtain the exact author-prepared analysis files and definitions, then verify the panel, municipal issue match, and both separate election branches against the supplied code.
steps: Request CKM.dta, new_issues_emma.dta, CKM_local.dta, and CKM_congress.dta in their author-prepared formats, with data dictionaries, identifiers, dates, and field definitions.

For CKM.dta, preserve dbkey and dbkey1 as distinct fields until the authors document their relationship; confirm all code-consumed columns, types, audit-year coverage, and the t−1, contiguous t−1 through t−4, and t+1 input windows. Keep the documented FAC 1999–2016 source period separate from those construction windows.

For new_issues_emma.dta, confirm the intended product and whether it is the prepared file behind the datasheet’s SDC-based municipal issuer match; document the local-government name/state/city/ZIP crosswalk, issue-year definition, and unique dbkey-audityear key. Do not substitute the generic SDC WRDS new-issues table or a corporate bond product.

For CKM_local.dta and CKM_congress.dta, document their separate year1 panels, the construction and meaning of lead_rvotes and pc1_finrep_lag, and the distinct local versus congressional tenure inputs; retain both branches.

If a compatible prepared input cannot be supplied, request the actual producer procedures and crosswalks for the relevant city/county, district, committee-membership, bond-issuer, and court/DOJ links. Treat that reconstruction as a conditional fallback, not as additional mandatory raw-source inputs while prepared author data remain the primary route.
validation: Use bounded metadata/readability inspection for each received Stata file. Compare actual source fields and types with expected_fields, verify dbkey-audityear uniqueness in both merge inputs, and inspect government, county/city, district, committee and year mappings.

Check date coverage and lead/lag edge availability from the actual inputs without inferring a minimum start year from the broad source-period statement. Do not use transcript counts or identifier listings as analysis data or completeness evidence.
